description: The movement contract (PL.movement-contract, U94(4); the Unreal P7 cell's m4, m5 and m6): what each camera mode does about a solid between the player and the lens (an overhead lens hides it), what blocks the player on a side view's strip and how a building's solid is read from the IR, what the world (isometric) and view frames mean for the move input, the run speed, and the slope and step limits. Data in, decision out: the engine's physics, sweep and renderer act on it.

occlusion.sightLine: the segment from the pivot (the feet plus the mode's pivotHeightM) to the lens (the pivot, back along the view by distanceM, then the offset)
occlusion.hide: every building solid the sight line touches is not drawn while it touches it and is drawn again once it does not; the player and the conversation partner are never hidden; listed nearest the pivot first (ties by id)
occlusion.props: a solid of kind prop (a lot's edge wall, a lamp post, a bench, street furniture) is never hidden by the lens, whatever its height, and is not hidden with its lot's building; it still blocks the player (the side view's strip). A solid that states no kind is a building
occlusion.pieces: a building may be stated as several solids, its drawn pieces (the walls, a flat roof's slab, a porch): each is hidden on its own while the sight line touches it, and hiding one hides no other. A building's solid from the IR is its walls piece
occlusion.pitchedRoof: not pinned (needs_ruling): how a pitched roof's piece is stated, as a roof-aware solid or as several boxes. The IR states no roof and a solid is a box; one box over a pitched roof lists the sight lines that pass over its slopes
occlusion.pullIn: the boom's own sweep (CAMERA_MODE_PARAMETERS.third_person.collision): the lens comes in front of the solid, never nearer than collision.minDistanceM; nothing is hidden
occlusion.none: the eye sits at the pivot: there is no sight line to clear
occlusion.viewYaw: the sight line is read at the mode's fixed yaw, else the view yaw given, else the mode's opening yaw; a mode that opens on the player's facing (first_person, third_person) given no view yaw is refused (error missing-view-yaw), as the move is

Pieces: ProceduralBuildingGenerator.ts:791-805 (the walls, one box width × floors·4 m × depth) and createRoof :893-943 (the roof, its own mesh). Unreal's follow arm keeps its sweep (pull-in), which the table already carries

contract.solid: a box standing on the ground: at (its base centre), halfWidthM across and halfDepthM along its facing, rotation (radians, the IR yaw: forward (sin r, cos r), right (cos r, −sin r)), heightM, and kind (optional: building, the default, or prop; any other kind is unreadable); every number finite, every extent > 0. A building's solid from the IR: spec.width × spec.depth about position, turned by rotation, max(1, floor(spec.floors)) × storeyM tall (its walls piece); no solid when width or depth is not a positive number
contract.sideView: plane xy: the player walks the line z = its own z. A solid whose footprint comes within the body radius of that line blocks the strip from xMin to xMax (the footprint clipped to the band z ± radius); the player passes over its top only (a jump, or a step when topY − the ground <= ground.stepUpM). Solids off the line are walked past; sorted by xMin, then id

frame.axes: the IR's world frame: metres, left-handed, +Y up; forward is +Z, right is +X, which is the player's right while facing +Z (one statement in a left-handed frame)
frame.world: the move input is read in the world frame whatever the view's yaw: forward moves along +Z and right along +X. Orbiting the lens (the look input, yaw orbit) never changes how the input maps. At the opening view (yaw 0) forward is screen-up and right is screen-right
frame.view: the move input is read in the view's frame: forward along the view's yaw (sin ψ, 0, cos ψ), right along (cos ψ, 0, −sin ψ). Under a fixed yaw of 180° right is −X, which is screen-right
frame.isometric: isometric: a perspective lens (not orthographic), pitch −45° at rest within [−60°, −30°], 25 m from a pivot 1.6 m above the feet (zoom 15–50 m), the yaw orbiting under the look input and opening at 0; the player moves on x and z (plane free: y is gravity and the jump), in the world frame
frame.input: the input (forward, right) is clamped to length 1 first (a stick past its rim, or two keys, is length 1), turned into the frame, then the plane drops its component (xy: z; xz: y); so a diagonal in a side view keeps only its x part, as Babylon's avatar walks its facing and loses the z
frame.mirroredLevel: an engine whose level mirrors the IR (Unreal's X = x, Y = z) keeps the player's right: right moves the player screen-right at the opening view, which is the image of the IR's −X in that level; it maps the answers here through its import

gait.source: babylon bfcdeb2 packages/babylon/src/engine/game-engine/rendering/BabylonGame.ts:10771-10772 (setWalkSpeed(2.5), setRunSpeed(5): run is twice the walk)

ground.source: babylon bfcdeb2 packages/babylon/src/engine/game-engine/rendering/BabylonGame.ts:10769-10770 (setStepOffset(0.75), setSlopeLimit(15, 75)); CharacterController.ts:1463-1521 _doIdle (:1491-1497 and :1512-1518: slope <= the lower limit (_sl1) grounded, else ungrounded and slideBack, with no test of the upper limit), :1138-1153 _doMove (>= the upper limit (_sl2) going up: moved back to where it started; above the lower: slowed), the step offset (a rise > stepOffset is refused)

contract.slope: slopeDeg in [0, 90], the player moving: <= standMaxDeg walk (walked, stood on); < climbMaxDeg slide (walked up slowed, slid down when idle); else blocked (not gone up: a step up it is undone; slid down when idle, as slopeAtRest says). Anything else is unreadable (null)
contract.slideSlowing: not pinned (needs_ruling): how much slower a slide slope is walked up. Babylon scales no walk by the slope (_doMove moves walk.speed · dt on any ground); going up a face steeper than standMaxDeg it only leaves its fall clock running (_movFallTime, not reset there as _endFreeFall resets it on walkable ground), so the pull down grows with the time on the face. That is a physics behaviour, not a factor core can state
contract.slopeAtRest: slopeDeg in [0, 90], the player not moving: <= standMaxDeg stand (grounded, stays put); else slideBack (slides down the slope under gravity until it stands on ground no steeper than standMaxDeg), the blocked slopes at or above climbMaxDeg included: the climb limit plays no part at rest (Babylon _doIdle reads only the lower limit). Anything else is unreadable (null)
contract.step: riseM: <= 0 none; <= stepUpM step; else blocked. Not a number: null
contract.order: answers do not depend on the order of solids or exclude

cases.name: occluders: side view, a house between the lens and the player is hidden (the Smithy case)
cases.note: Unreal's P7 cell: every -side run opened "hidden behind Denham's Smithy". The overhead lens is not moved; the house is not drawn while it stands on the sight line.

occluders: side view, two houses on the line, nearest the player first
occluders: side view, a wall below the sight line is drawn
cases.note: The sight line runs 1.6 m up (the pivot). A 1.2 m wall stays under it; a 1.8 m wall crosses it and is hidden.

cases.name: occluders: side view, a turned house reaches the line its unturned footprint misses
cases.note: Both are 4 m squares 2.5 m off the line; turned 45° the corner reaches 0.33 m past it.

cases.name: occluders: side view, a long wall turned +30° meets the line at its near end
cases.note: The IR yaw turns +Z toward +X: at +30° the wall's −Z end swings toward −X and crosses the line nearer the player.

cases.note: The lens 12 m out on +Z, pitched −8.18°: it rises 1.71 m over the 12 m.

cases.name: occluders: isometric at its opening yaw, a two-storey house south of the player is hidden
cases.note: At yaw 0 the lens is on the −Z side, 25 m back at −45°: the sight line climbs 1 m per metre south.

occluders: top-down, the player in a doorway inside a footprint hides that building at 0 m
occluders: third person pulls in, nothing is hidden
cases.note: The boom's own sweep brings the lens in front of the wall (collision 0.3 m probe, 1.4 m nearest).

cases.name: occluders: first person has no sight line to clear
cases.note: A follow mode is read at the view yaw the host gives (here 0); with none it is refused (the next cases).

cases.name: occluders: first person with no view yaw is refused, as the move is
cases.note: A follow mode opens on the player's facing, so core has no yaw of its own to read the lens at: missing-view-yaw (PL.movement-followups, U95(5)), never yaw 0.

cases.name: occluders: third person with no view yaw is refused, as the move is
occluders: third person with a view yaw that is not a number is refused
occluders: side view, a lot's 3.6 m edge wall (a prop) on the sight line stays drawn; the house beyond it is hidden
cases.note: The wall crosses the sight line 2 m out and stands 2 m over it. Babylon hides only pickable meshes, and every prop is made non-pickable (it keeps its collision), so the lens hides the house and draws the wall.

cases.name: occluders: side view, the lens inside its lot's edge wall: the restaurant on the line is hidden, the wall is not hidden with it
cases.note: The Unreal P7 critic's drawn-again stand (run 10, round 3, m1): the lens 15 m out stands inside the restaurant lot's edge wall. A prop is not hidden under its lot's building: the frame shows the wall.

cases.name: occluders: isometric, the Town Square's 4 m lamp post (a prop) on the sight line stays drawn
cases.note: At yaw 0 the sight line is 3.1 m up where it passes the post, under its 4 m top. Babylon's TownSquareGenerator makes the lamp post non-pickable, so its lens never hides it.

cases.name: occluders: isometric, the same post stated as a building is hidden, as a solid with no kind is
occluders: a solid of a kind the contract does not name is unreadable
occluders: isometric, a one-storey shop stated as walls and flat roof: only the roof the sight line touches is hidden
cases.note: The sight line passes 4.35 m up over the walls' near edge (4 m) and through the slab's overhang (4 to 4.5 m). Babylon hides each mesh it picks on its own.

cases.name: occluders: side view, the Smithy stated as walls and flat roof: the walls are hidden, the roof above the sight line stays drawn
cases.note: The level sight line runs 1.6 m up, through the walls and under the slab at 4 to 4.5 m: hiding the walls does not hide the roof.

cases.name: sideView: a house across the player's line blocks the strip; one behind the line does not
cases.note: The Smithy stands 5 m off the line: the player walks past in front of it (and the lens hides it).

sideView: the body's radius decides a near miss
cases.note: Their near faces stand 0.4 m and 0.5 m off the line; the body reaches 0.42 m.
